This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Learn how to accept credit card payments using meses sin intereses across a variety of Stripe products.
Installments only works with `payment` mode, not `setup` or `subscription` mode.
After an installment plan is set on a PaymentIntent, it remains until you remove it.
You can enable installments for individual invoices but not for subscriptions.

findings: November retains the guide purpose and supplies six route links. May has five full variant bodies, including No code/Payment Links. No substantive operational difference follows from replacement by the index (old raw lines 4-22 and new raw lines 5-18).

The new Terminal URL is an additional navigation route (new raw lines 13-18 versus old raw lines 24-26, 78-80, 134-136, 499-501 and 725-727). The separate November Mexico overview explicitly lists Terminal at raw/stripe-payments-mx-installments-2026-11-07.md:9-11. That corroborates product-level documentation only. The linked Terminal body was not used, and neither this index nor the overview establishes a release date, specific Terminal SDK, device, flow, country or account eligibility beyond that overview's stated Mexico requirements.

May describes ordinary one-time merchant charge treatment with fees and issuer collection from the cardholder over billing statements (old raw lines 16-20). Separate Mexico overview requirements are Stripe Mexico account, MXN, supported Mexican-issued consumer credit card and plan-specific amount thresholds, with an ordinary payout schedule (raw/stripe-payments-mx-installments-2026-11-07.md:9-37,78-101).

May's Checkout Sessions `payment` route and Payment Element PaymentIntent route make explicit enablement conditional on not using dynamic payment methods, subject to eligibility. Payment Element gives the browser a client secret and confirms with `confirmPayment`; its historical warning says setting enabled=false with dynamic methods may error. Historical issuer decline codes may indicate an unsupported selected plan, with retry on another plan or without installments (old raw lines 24-70, 78-126).

Old raw lines 138-146, 179-216, 244-261, 314-436 and 491-497 document a client-created card PaymentMethod, an unconfirmed MXN PaymentIntent created on the server to retrieve `available_plans`, client choice of a plan or immediate payment, and later server confirmation of that same Intent. Explicitly unset a previously saved `plan` when reconfirming without installments, including after switching to an ineligible card. The sample endpoint's `success: true` accompanies a returned status and the UI only treats `succeeded` as success. The separate PaymentIntent schema enumerates intermediate states (raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-object-2026-11-07.md:715-737).

For individual invoices the May server examples first create an `InvoiceItem` with the Price in `pricing.price`, then separately create the `Invoice` with `pending_invoice_items_behavior: 'include'` and `collection_method: 'send_invoice'`. Both calls use `customer_account` for an Accounts v2 customer-configured Account or `customer` for a Customers v1 Customer. May describes Accounts v2 as generally available to Connect users and in public preview for other users, with a preview version required for preview participants. Hosted plans require an eligible card and at least 300 MXN, but plans have separate settings and eligibility. No-code Payment Links uses Dashboard enablement. Plan minimum/maximum settings apply across compatible existing installment integrations (old raw lines 8-14, 511-620, 695-758).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Use May 1, 2026 for the full capture even though its filename says 2025. Retain the five behavior routes, May Accounts v2 conditions, client/server split, API modes, card/transaction/issuer qualifications, plan persistence and unset, historical Dahlia-hosted Stripe.js sample, no-code settings and sandbox card results (old raw lines 2-22, 38-70, 92-153, 179-261, 314-497, 511-758).

Capture and version-qualify object shapes from the May examples separately from the documented API changelog. Preserve issuer collection versus merchant charge/timing and the additional fee, rather than construing examples or client selection as live payment or settlement (old raw lines 16-20, 370-489, 624-693).
conflicts: Baseline source lines 17 and 19 can be read as requiring the flag for dynamic methods, while May describes conditional manual enablement and says to leave the Payment Element flag unset when dynamic methods are in use (old raw lines 38-42, 92-126). Source line 23 gives 300 MXN alone, while the hosted page requires a supported credit card with total >=300 MXN (old raw lines 612-622) and separate issuer/plan thresholds apply. Source line 27 needs the 'compatible existing installment integrations' scope (old raw lines 695-701, 737-749).

Replace source line 21's Japan shorthand and vague 'gotcha' with the Mexican direct API state sequence and explicit unsetting rule, and qualify the broad Accounts v2 claim at source line 13 against May raw lines 8-14 and 532-610. Direct example confirmation or success response wrapper alone does not establish a successful payment.

Old raw lines 443-489 and 624-693 depict `PaymentIntent.charges.data` and a direct Invoice-to-PaymentIntent field. Preserve the sample provenance with version warnings. The 2022-11-15 changelog removes `PaymentIntent.charges` in favor of `latest_charge` (raw/stripe-changelog-2022-11-15-removes-charges-attribute-paymentintent-2026-11-07.md:5-24), and `2025-03-31.basil` removes `Invoice.payment_intent` and uses the Invoice Payment relationship, which can represent multiple payments (raw/stripe-changelog-basil-2025-03-31-add-support-for-multiple-partial-payments-on-invoices-2026-11-07.md:5-44,58-66). These are separate dated API changes and are absent from the November integration index.

Both Mexico overviews report recurring payments 'Yes' at their product-property level (raw/stripe-mx-installments-2025.md:26-36 and raw/stripe-payments-mx-installments-2026-11-07.md:27-37). Keep a reciprocal scope warning in Stripe Installments. The May integration explicitly limits Checkout to `payment` and Invoicing to individual `send_invoice` invoices, excluding subscriptions and automatic invoice collection (old raw lines 38-42, 511-536). The overview property does not establish those excluded routes or specify an eligible recurring integration.
unresolved_questions: This canonical capture does not contain any November variant implementation bodies. Terminal-specific steps, version/SDK compatibility for an account and actual live plan/payment availability remain outside the reviewed evidence.

source_assessments.reason: No raw behavioral delta. Existing abbreviated prerequisites and consequential plan, state and API-version distinctions independently warrant correction.

answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meses-sin-intereses/accept-a-payment identifies acceptance of meses sin intereses credit card payments and lists Checkout, Elements, Direct API, Invoices, No code (Payment Links) and Terminal. It supplies routes only (new raw lines 5-18). The May 1 guide documents a Mexico consumer credit card purchase split over billing statements, with issuer collection and normal merchant charge treatment after fees. It describes payment-mode Checkout and Payment Element with dynamic or manual configuration, and a Direct API flow where the client creates a PaymentMethod, the server retrieves available plans on an unconfirmed MXN PaymentIntent, the client chooses a plan or immediate payment, then the server confirms the same Intent. Plan lookup, card choice and confirmation request acceptance precede payment success. For individual invoices the May server examples first create an `InvoiceItem` with the Price in `pricing.price`, then separately create the `Invoice` with `pending_invoice_items_behavior: 'include'` and `collection_method: 'send_invoice'`. Both calls use `customer_account` for an Accounts v2 customer-configured Account or `customer` for a Customers v1 Customer. The hosted UI only shows plans on eligible cards for totals at least 300 MXN, subject to plan configuration. Payment Links uses Dashboard enablement. See old raw lines 8-22, old raw lines 38-126, old raw lines 138-261, old raw lines 370-497, old raw lines 511-622 and old raw lines 695-758. source-stripe-mx-installments-accept-payment.md summarizes the five May variants. Its shorthand needs the dynamic-method, issuer eligibility, Accounts v2 preview and plan-reset qualifications.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meses-sin-intereses/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-18 repeat the purpose and provide navigation, adding a Terminal route beyond May's five documented sections. The separate November Mexico overview lists Terminal as a product-level route. No reviewed Terminal body establishes the SDK steps or a launch date. source-stripe-mx-installments-accept-payment.md should retain the May 1, 2026 behavior, including payment-mode Checkout, dynamic versus manual flags, direct client PaymentMethod/server PaymentIntent timing, explicit unsetting of a persistent plan, Invoicing's eligible-card and amount restrictions, Accounts v2 preview/version boundaries, and sandbox examples (old raw lines 8-14, old raw lines 38-126, old raw lines 138-261, old raw lines 409-497, old raw lines 511-622 and old raw lines 725-758). Scope the overview's recurring property in the reciprocal Stripe Installments route to avoid applying it to May's excluded subscription modes. Old raw lines 443-489 and old raw lines 624-693 have legacy lookup examples. Separate dated changelogs identify latest_charge in place of PaymentIntent.charges and the 2025-03-31.basil Invoice Payment relationship in place of the old Invoice.payment_intent field. A redirect, an available plan, the illustrative response wrapper, and sandbox card results cannot establish live payment success, access or settlement.
